front_prompt: 2. What are the three main components of a map? Explain each briefly.
back_answer: The three components are: (1) Distance (represented using a scale, which is the ratio of map distance to ground distance), (2) Direction (indicated using cardinal N, S, E, W and intermediate NE, SE, SW, NW directions), and (3) Symbols (standardized visual icons representing physical and human features like roads, bridges, and post offices).
